decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3: “save a URL quickly”; client entry 4 confirms saving should feel quick.
decisions.note: Conforming discovery-stage decision to save bookmarks by URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3 presents finding bookmarks “by searching or by tags”; client entry 4 specifies address/title/description/note search without capitalization sensitivity.
decisions.note: Conforming discovery-stage search and tag-filter direction.

decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3 presents notes, read-later, and archiving without main-view clutter; client entry 4 approves the direction.
decisions.note: Conforming discovery-stage organization decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3: an already-saved link should return to the existing item “instead of making a duplicate”; client entry 4 approves the direction.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-save rule at discovery stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, maker entry 5 presents the always-visible URL box and Save action; client entry 6 says the placement and clearing behavior feel right.
decisions.note: Conforming prototype decision for URL saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, maker entry 5 presents automatic lookup only through the filled title and short description; client entry 6 adds that each item should show “its favicon.”
decisions.note: At prototype review, the presented metadata set omitted the favicon requirement and the client surfaced it.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, maker entry 5 presents automatic title/description collection and asks whether anything is missing; client entry 6 requests favicon but does not mention a preview image.
decisions.note: The automatic metadata presentation omitted preview-image collection, and that facet passed unexpressed in this review.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, maker entry 5 says each list item shows “title, the address, and a short description”; client entry 6 adds “favicon and any tags at a glance.”
decisions.note: The initial list-item decision omitted two required readability fields; the client supplied them.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, maker entry 5 presents the saved item without navigation behavior; client entry 6 states, “The title should open the original page when I select it.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing original-URL navigation behavior during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, maker entry 5 presents auto-filled title/description without a correction affordance; client entry 6 requests “a way to correct the title or description.”
decisions.note: The client added post-save correction of automatically collected fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 presents a favicon position, de-emphasized address, and title opening the original page; client entry 8 confirms all three feel right.
decisions.note: Revised list-item presentation conforms to readability and navigation requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 presents post-save title and description editing; client entry 8 accepts the item while requesting additional pre-save editing.
decisions.note: The presented after-save editing behavior conforms for title and description.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7: “The description field doubles as where your own notes go”; client entry 8 says notes must be separate and viewable with formatting such as lists or links.
decisions.note: The client replaced a combined description/note model with the reference-conforming independent markdown note.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 only demonstrates editing after save; client entry 8 adds that title and description must be correctable “before confirming the save, as well as afterward.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing pre-save editing stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 defines “Edit details” as title/description fields; client entry 8 discusses notes and pre-save correction but does not request URL editing here.
decisions.note: The presented editor omitted URL editing, and that difference passed unexpressed at this prototype review; it was later raised at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, maker entry 9 presents three functionally equivalent pre-save review flows, all allowing title/description adjustment; client entry 10 selects the expanding-panel version.
decisions.note: All offered alternatives fulfill pre-save editing; the layout preference is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, maker entry 9 presents a separate note with rendered list/link syntax and preview; client entry 10 says it works as pictured and needs no toolbar.
decisions.note: Conforming separate markdown-note decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, maker entry 11 presents case-insensitive search across address, title, description, and note; client entry 12 confirms the span and behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming basic full-text search decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, maker entry 11 presents clickable tag filters, including match-all narrowing for multiple tags; client entry 12 accepts that behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming tag-filter decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, maker entry 11 presents “type-a-word-and-press-Enter” tag entry; client entry 12 says it “should suggest existing tags as I type.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing existing-tag autocomplete requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, maker entry 11 presents basic text search and separate tag chips; client entry 12 requests typing tags directly as “#tag.”
decisions.note: The client added tag syntax to the search language.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, maker entry 11 presents only basic text search; client entry 12 requests searching “an exact phrase in quotes.”
decisions.note: The client added exact quoted-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, maker entry 11 presents only basic search and tag chips; client entry 12 requests “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing Boolean and grouping search language.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, maker entry 13 demonstrates “#read-later” and quoted exact phrases; client entry 14 says typed-tag and exact-phrase searches behave as expected.
decisions.note: Revised power-search presentation conforms for tag and phrase syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, maker entry 13 demonstrates AND/OR/NOT and parenthesized grouping; client entry 14 accepts exclusions and grouped searches.
decisions.note: Conforming Boolean/grouping behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, maker entry 13 lists Boolean/grouping examples but does not define quoted operator words; client entry 14 explicitly states operators should be ordinary words when quoted. Round 15, maker entry 29 incorporates that rule.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing literal-operator rule; its later incorporation resolves the same decision rather than creating a separate pending decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, maker entry 13 presents existing-tag suggestions with keyboard selection and a create-new option; client entry 14 confirms the reuse problem is solved.
decisions.note: Revised tag-entry presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, maker entry 15 presents a read-later toggle, separate To read view, and unmarking; client entry 16 says this treatment feels right.
decisions.note: Conforming unread/read-later flow.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, maker entry 15 hides archived items from All and To read, provides an Archived view, and allows unarchiving; client entry 16 confirms this behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming archive visibility and archive-list decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, maker entry 15 has duplicate saving jump to and briefly highlight the existing item; client entry 16 says it should instead “open that bookmark for editing.”
decisions.note: Highlight-only handling did not guide the user into editing; the client supplied the conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, maker entry 17 revises duplicate handling to open the existing bookmark editor; client entry 18 confirms it matches the intended behavior.
decisions.note: Revised duplicate-save decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, maker entry 19 proposes refusing empty/invalid addresses with an explanatory note; client entry 20 agrees that invalid input should save nothing.
decisions.note: Conforming URL-required validation decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, maker entry 19 proposes graceful wrapping for long titles, notes, and many tags; client entry 20 confirms that expectation.
decisions.note: Conforming readability behavior at this review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, maker entry 21 proposes newest-first ordering as the default while preparing to close scope; client entry 22 says it “shouldn’t be the only ordering” and requests date/title sorting.
decisions.note: The client added the missing user-selectable sorting capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, maker entry 23 presents newest, oldest, title A–Z, and title Z–A sorting within active filters/views; client entry 24 says those cover the main ways to sort.
decisions.note: Revised sort-key decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, maker entry 23 presents a temporary sort dropdown without a default-sort preference; client entry 24 requests that ordering be remembered or configurable as the default.
decisions.note: The client added the missing default-sort setting.

decisions.evidence: Round 13, maker entry 25 implements “remember your last choice” and explicitly offers an alternative default-sort setting; client entry 26 selects the explicit setting because temporary browsing changes should not rewrite the default.
decisions.note: The offered remembered-last-choice behavior diverged from the reference profile setting; the client selected the conforming alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 14, maker entry 27 separates a deliberate Settings default from temporary dropdown overrides; client entry 28 confirms this matches the intended model.
decisions.note: Revised default and temporary sorting behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 calls the summarized scope complete but includes reversible Archive and no delete; client entry 30 requires permanent delete “clearly distinguished from reversible archiving.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client added permanent deletion and its distinction from archive.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 says saved details can be corrected but does not include the URL; client entry 30 specifies that editing must include “the saved address itself.”
decisions.note: The client caught the missing URL-edit requirement at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 presents only per-item actions; client entry 30 requests selecting several bookmarks to tag, mark read/unread, archive, or delete together.
decisions.note: The client added missing multi-bookmark actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 contains no whole-result bulk action; client entry 30 requests acting on “everything matching the current search/view.”
decisions.note: The client added the current-filter-scoped whole-collection action.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 has search and tag filters but no reusable saved filter; client entry 30 requests saving search terms and included/excluded tags as a collection.
decisions.note: The client added the missing bundle/saved-filter feature.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 omits preserved content; client entry 30 requests a local page copy and specifies that PDFs retain the PDF itself.
decisions.note: The client added local HTML/PDF snapshot preservation.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 omits public archival; client entry 30 requests an Internet Archive copy option.
decisions.note: The client added the missing Internet Archive feature.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 contains no import; client entry 30 requests importing standard browser-bookmark HTML while retaining title, tags, and original date.
decisions.note: The client added Netscape HTML import.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 contains no export; client entry 30 requests exporting standard browser-bookmark HTML.
decisions.note: The client added Netscape HTML export.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 includes only default sort in Settings; client entry 30 requests settings for font size and displayed-item count.
decisions.note: The client added the missing display-related profile settings.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 summarizes automatic title/summary collection and a site icon but no preview image; client entry 30 requires collecting the real site icon and preview image where available.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client caught the remaining automatic-metadata gap, especially preview-image collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 defers handling very long content as later polish; client entry 30 states ordinary long titles, notes, and many tags wrapping cleanly is part of this build’s basic readability.
decisions.note: The client rejected deferral of ordinary readability behavior while allowing large-collection performance work to remain later.

decisions.evidence: Round 16, maker entry 31 presents guarded permanent delete adjacent to reversible Archive; client entry 32 approves the confirmation and permanent wording.
decisions.note: Revised delete/archive decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 16, maker entry 31 presents validated URL editing and refusal when the target URL already exists; client entry 32 approves leaving both bookmarks unchanged and explaining the conflict.
decisions.note: Conforming URL-edit and uniqueness decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, maker entry 33 revises delete placement while retaining permanent confirmation; client entry 34 settles the block.
decisions.note: The revised presentation preserves conforming delete/archive semantics; visual placement itself is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, maker entry 33 names the conflicting bookmark and leaves both unchanged on duplicate URL edits; client entry 34 confirms this behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming address-conflict behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, maker entry 35 presents bulk add/remove tag, “Mark read later,” archive, and delete but no inverse read action; client entry 36 says bulk “Mark as read” is still missing.
decisions.note: The initial bulk-action set omitted the required read action.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, maker entry 35 defines “Select all N shown” as all bookmarks matching the current search/view; client entry 36 confirms it must include search, tag filters, and view.
decisions.note: Conforming current-filter scope for whole-result actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 19, maker entry 37 adds bulk Mark as read and retains exact filtered scope; client entry 38 says both read states and Select all shown now match the intended behavior.
decisions.note: Revised bulk-action block conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 20, maker entry 39 saves search text plus included tags, preserving exclusions as NOT #tag and reapplying the filter; client entry 40 confirms the combination and explicitly requires live results.
decisions.note: Conforming dynamic bundle implementation; encoding excluded tags in the search term is functionally equivalent.

decisions.evidence: Round 21, maker entry 41 presents an offline local page copy and stores a PDF itself for PDF URLs; client entry 42 confirms self-contained pages and direct PDF storage.
decisions.note: Conforming local snapshot and PDF rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 21, maker entry 41 presents creation and opening of an Internet Archive copy; client entry 42 wants the feature and adds a public-nature warning.
decisions.note: The core Internet Archive capability conforms; the warning is an additional safety preference outside the reference item.

decisions.evidence: Round 22, maker entry 43 presents self-contained local copies, PDF storage, optional auto-capture, failure safety, and confirmed public Archive creation; client entry 44 settles the block.
decisions.note: Revised preservation block conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23, maker entry 45 presents Netscape-format import preserving titles, tags, and dates; client entry 46 confirms the format and fields.
decisions.note: Conforming import decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 23, maker entry 45 presents Netscape-format export with title, TAGS, and ADD_DATE; client entry 46 confirms standard-field export is acceptable.
decisions.note: Conforming export decision; omission of private notes/states from the standard interchange format does not diverge from the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 24, maker entry 47 presents text-size and displayed-items/page settings alongside default sort; client entry 48 says the offered choices are sufficient.
decisions.note: Conforming display-related personal settings.

decisions.evidence: Round 25, maker entry 49 presents actual favicon loading with fallback and a preview image only where available; client entry 50 confirms both the recognition and list layout.
decisions.note: Revised favicon/preview metadata and display decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 26, maker entry 51 presents the revised complete scope containing delete, URL editing, bulk actions, saved collections, preservation, import/export, and settings; client entry 52 says the complete scope matches and authorizes implementation.
decisions.note: Conforming final specification-gate decision after the prior corrections.

decisions.evidence: Round 27, maker entry 53 presents the finished application as implementing the approved behavior and explicitly discloses that online success of external-service paths was not exercised; client entry 54 accepts the software and the disclosed verification limitation.
decisions.note: The acceptance-stage behavior presented is reference-conforming. The external-network caveat is verification uncertainty, not a presented functional departure, so it is not an accepted divergence.
